newsitem.title: USA: US Senate Democrat chief hopeful on budget session.
newsitem.headline: US Senate Democrat chief hopeful on budget session.

text.p: Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle said Wednesday he was "very hopeful" that budget negotiations in the afternoon between congressional budget leaders and President Clinton would be "productive."
"I'm hopeful that we can see some real movement as a result of progress this afternoon," Daschle told reporters.
The South Dakota Republican also said it was unlikely that the consumer price index issue would be part of early budget negotiations.

"I don't think there's much possibility it (CPI) will be revived at any time in the early stages of the budget negotiations," Daschle told reporters. He added there was "too much opposition" to the issue.
An advisory commission headed by economist Michael Boskin determined late last year that the CPI overstated cost of living by about 1.1 percentage points a year.
Since then some congressional leaders have advocated setting up a commission to study how to fix the overstatement, while others oppose any congressional action on CPI.
Reducing the inflation measure would make it easier to balance the budget because it would mean reduced spending for some federal benefits that have increases tied to CPI.
